findings: All 24 primary 100 ms, 24 dense 20 ms and eight alternate-cadence controls complete. All 24 original 20 ms record hashes are unchanged. Shared prefixes, alternate-cadence shared frames, final node states and summaries agree exactly.
Recorded damping increments are positive; all pass the declared 1e-12 J monotonicity tolerance. Contact work remains signed.

At the finest step, rear-wheel time-weighted sampled RMS speed increases across the five bins, while front samples remain phase/cadence sensitive. This does not establish equilibrium or asymptotic instability.

Changing only recording cadence from 500 to 625 us changes hardtail-front retained-rate 20–40 ms sampled RMS speed from 0.00101164 to 0.00141792 m/s (about 40%), despite exact shared frames and final state. These time means/RMS are quadrature estimates of saved samples.
Fine/finest front-node and contact-load differences remain material. All-step energy residuals also accumulate; smaller residuals at smaller dt do not establish converged motion.
next: Add bounded interval statistics at every accepted integration step and a dense late observation window; compare those against saved-sample estimates before constitutive damping changes. Preserve replay, progress, accepted-prefix rollback and no-allocation inner-loop constraints. Then return to whole-bike perturbation/60 s idle and rider control gates.
